einzeiler: Germany's descent into post-WWI turmoil, revolutionary violence, and the birth of the…
kurzfassung: As World War I ended, defeated Germany and Austria faced spreading communist revolutions, mass starvation under ongoing Allied blockades, and economic collapse. Radicals like Karl Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg attempted to spark a Bolshevik-style civil war, leading to brutal street battles in Berlin. Disillusioned front soldiers and volunteer Freikorps militias ultimately crushed the insurrections with extreme violence, setting the stage for radical political extremism.
stichpunkte: Germany faced unexpected military defeat in late 1918, followed rapidly by the collapse of allied empires and domestic revolutions.
The Allied hunger blockade continued after the armistice, causing hundreds of thousands of civilian deaths from starvation in Germany and Austria.
News of atrocities and the total breakdown of society during the Bolshevik revolution in Russia terrified the German middle class and military.
German radicals Karl Liebknecht and Rosa Luxemburg led the Spartacist movement, attempting to import a bloody Soviet-style revolution to Germany.
Tensions boiled over during 'Bloody Friday' in December 1918, resulting in deadly street clashes between protesters, soldiers, and sailors.
A makeshift provisional government under Friedrich Ebert struggled to maintain order without reliable state forces or functioning police.
The returning frontline soldiers were profoundly alienated from civilian society, viewing ordinary citizens and revolutionaries with cold detachment and hostility.
Freikorps militias were officially authorized and unleashed to brutally suppress communist uprisings, culminating in the execution of Liebknecht and Luxemburg.

clips.text: By the autumn of 1918, American forces were suffering 25,000 casualties every week despite having little direct stake in the conflict.

clips.hook: Jewish participation in the German army
clips.text: Official records show that out of 100,000 mobilized German Jews, approximately 70,000 actively served on the front lines.

clips.hook: Bolshevik executions versus the Tsarist regime
clips.text: The Bolsheviks carried out more than 6,000 executions in just two months, nearly matching the entire death sentence total of the Tsarist regime over 92 years.
Returning soldiers marched through cities with cold detachment, viewing patriotic slogans as empty shams and feeling entirely disconnected from civilian life.
Following her capture in a Berlin hotel, Rosa Luxemburg was beaten senseless by a hostile crowd, shot in the head, and dumped into a canal.

beschreibung:
Over the span of a handful of months, the most ancient ruling houses of Europe collapsed under the weight of deprivation and suffering brought about by the Great War. As communist revolutionaries burn Russia to the ground, their comrades preach blood and fire on the streets of Berlin, and while the Allied countries celebrate their noble victory, the starving, exhausted people of the German Reich face a new enemy more terrible than any they faced in the trenches.
